- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot in the 10–15 day horizon following strong sentiment upturns.
- Underestimate when sentiment is persistently negative (especially > -0.5) — model fails to adjust downward sufficiently.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows; correct by smoothing out 3–5 day momentum in forecast tails.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns negative within 3 days, model delays correction — apply a 1–2 day lagged adjustment downward.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast slope after 10–12 days if sentiment is volatile.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often misreads direction; reduce forecast slope if sentiment < -0.3 and price > 80.
